transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi there! I'm feeling okay, thank you for asking. I do have a few questions about my recovery. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. Just be careful not to get any dirt or debris in your eyes. And remember to wear protective eyewear if you're doing anything that might splash or spray.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense. Thank you for the advice. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using the preservative-free eye drops for dryness four times daily. It's usually recommended to start using them as soon as you can, and continue as directed. If you're running low, your GP can provide more for you.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, I'll make sure to do that. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Yes, it's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light after surgery. If it's mild, just wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. But if it's severe or accompanied by redness and pain, we may need to check it further.
